<!--
  interview-debrief — JTBD four-forces debrief from a recent-switcher interview.
  Lives at: `domain/interviews/<kebab-name>.md`.
  Authorship: derived. SLO: never — a debrief records one interview at a point in time; it is not refreshed.
  Owner: fixed to `domain`, do not substitute.
  Discipline: JTBD invariants — subject is a recent switcher (≤60 days since hire/fire); the job is
    progress in a circumstance, stated solution-agnostically; the synthesized job statement names all
    three dimensions (functional, emotional, social); verbatim customer language preserved, never
    paraphrased as a quote.
  Variants: hybrid of Moesta's switch-interview four-forces method and Christensen's three-dimension
    job statement — recommended for solo-operator / founder scope.
  Extra frontmatter: `sources` MUST be non-empty and reference the transcript path under `_raw/`.
  Disposition: keep every header; "None." when empty.
  Substitute: {{TITLE}} {{DATE}} {{CONFIDENCE}} {{ORIGINATION}} {{INTERVIEW_DATE}}
    {{INTERVIEWER}} {{INTERVIEWEE_ROLE}} {{CIRCUMSTANCE}} {{TRANSCRIPT_PATH}}.
-->

## Interview context

<!-- Date of interview, interviewer name, interviewee role + the circumstance they were in when the switch happened. Reference the transcript via [[_raw:<path>]]. Sample:

- **Interview date:** {{INTERVIEW_DATE}}
- **Interviewer:** {{INTERVIEWER}}
- **Interviewee role:** {{INTERVIEWEE_ROLE}}
- **Circumstance:** {{CIRCUMSTANCE}}
- **Transcript:** [[_raw:{{TRANSCRIPT_PATH}}]]

Circumstance scopes the job — a "when": time, place, who-with, what-just-happened. Not a demographic. -->

## Recent switch identified

<!-- What was hired, what was fired, when. The four-forces framing only works on a recent switcher (see the JTBD invariants in the header); non-switchers produce self-justification, not insight. State concretely:

- **Solution hired:** what they switched to.
- **Solution fired:** what they switched from.
- **Switch date (approx):** when the switch happened.
- **Trigger event:** the specific moment that turned consideration into action.

If the subject is not a recent switcher, stop and move them to a separate loyalty study — this template does not apply. -->

## The four forces

### Push of the situation

<!-- What pushed them away from the old solution? Dissatisfaction, friction, a moment of insufficiency. Capture verbatim quotes — the customer's words carry the emotional and social signal. -->

### Pull of the new solution

<!-- What pulled them toward the alternative? The appeal, the promise, the demonstrated capability. Verbatim quotes. -->

### Anxieties

<!-- What slowed the switch? Worry about cost, risk, learning curve, what colleagues would think, what their boss would say. Anxieties are why customers don't switch even when they want to. Verbatim quotes. -->

### Habits

<!-- What anchored them to the old solution? Routines, sunk cost, "the way we've always done it", lateral dependencies. Habits are the silent counter-force. Verbatim quotes. -->

## Surfaced jobs

<!-- The synthesized job statement(s), in canonical form:

> "When [circumstance], help me [functional progress] so I [emotional outcome] and [social outcome]."

Per the JTBD invariants (header). One statement per circumstance (the morning milkshake and the afternoon milkshake are different jobs). Example:

> "When I'm commuting in the morning alone with nothing to do for thirty minutes, help me stay engaged and feel less bored so I show up to work alert."

Re-read each statement and grep for product, brand, or demographic names. Any hit means re-phrase as the underlying progress. -->
